releaseControl.candidateIdentity: The clean exact commit recorded by minimum-release evidence after implementation and review.

wholeProduct.summary: TradeScout earns organic discovery through a reachable canonical domain, a truthful crawl graph, substantive Trust/CVS-governed public profiles, authoritative acquisition telemetry, source-backed profile expansion, repeatable distribution, and measured conversion improvement.

deliverables.outcome: A search or referral visitor can reach the canonical TradeScout domain, discover only valid indexable public surfaces, enter a truthful public profile or acquisition page, take a signup action, and produce authoritative server-confirmed acquisition and registration evidence without weakening Trust/CVS or contact gating.
deliverables.entry: A crawler or visitor requests the canonical TradeScout domain or a URL emitted by a TradeScout sitemap.
deliverables.ending: The visitor reaches a substantive canonical page; completed registration and activation are reconciled from authoritative server state, while any signed public-discovery attribution is recorded as a separately measured fail-soft projection.
journeySteps: Resolve the apex and www hosts to one working HTTPS canonical domain.
Emit only canonical, rendered, substantive, internally linked, index-eligible URLs from sitemaps.
Apply one Trust/CVS-backed public discoverability contract consistently across SSR, sitemap, search, and client rendering.
Record landing, profile discovery, CTA, registration, and activation milestones with server-confirmed signup truth and bounded deduplication.
Verify the exact candidate through focused tests, minimum-release evidence, browser proof, independent objection, and production identity after any authorized release.

proof.procedure: Recursively inspect the live sitemap graph, sample every route class, compare rendered robots and canonicals, and test apex and www HTTPS reachability.
proof.expected: Every emitted URL is canonical, reachable, rendered, substantive, internally linked, and index-eligible, and both public hosts complete HTTPS with one canonical destination.
proof.observed: The baseline inspection found malformed city URLs, county hydration failures, sitemap-listed noindex and test artifacts, empty or generic bot bodies, and a failing apex HTTPS handshake; implementation evidence is not yet recorded.

proof.procedure: Run focused sitemap, SSR, discoverability, attribution, registration, and law-contract tests followed by the exact minimum-release gate and browser crawl-path proof.
proof.expected: The repaired crawl-to-signup loop passes with canonical server-side signup evidence and no Trust/CVS, contact, county, or authority regression.
proof.observed: At the baseline commit the reconciled recovery tests and exact-candidate release evidence do not yet exist, so this proof remains open.

constraints: Reuse canonical TradeScout routing, Trust/CVS, signup, analytics, and release owners; do not create parallel public identity or contact authority.
Visibility never grants contact or power, and every contact path remains Intent to Decision Card to Contact.
Unclaimed or ineligible profiles remain direct-link-only or noindex according to the canonical exposure policy.
Do not manufacture business facts, claims, locations, reviews, inventory, demand, or availability for SEO volume.
Do not merge stale PR 426 or PR 427 independently; reconcile their supported intent on current main.
Do not merge to main or claim production correction without exact-commit release evidence and authorized production action.

completionClaims.claim: The apex and www hosts complete HTTPS and resolve to one explicit canonical TradeScout destination.
TradeScout sitemaps emit only valid canonical URLs whose server-rendered result is substantive and index-eligible.
SSR, sitemap, search, and client routing apply one canonical public-profile discoverability decision without widening access.

Landing, discovery, and CTA projections are separated from authoritative completed-registration and activation state; projection and source-attribution coverage are reported without treating client intent or missing telemetry as a successful signup.
Trust/CVS, visibility, county, contact, verification, and authority invariants remain enforced across the repaired acquisition path.

excludedFromActive: Nationwide source-backed business profile creation and enrichment beyond repairing the current eligibility and discovery machinery.
Scaled partnership, media, outbound, referral, and content distribution campaigns.
Conversion-rate optimization, paid acquisition, lifecycle messaging, and growth experimentation after trustworthy traffic and funnel data exist.
Unrelated Community, JW Stone, Direct Connect, admin, marketplace, and product-surface changes.

deliverables.outcome: Expand source-backed, claimable, Trust/CVS-governed public business coverage without fabricated facts or automatic contact access.
Operate a repeatable distribution system across partnerships, editorial surfaces, earned links, referrals, and owned channels.
Use trustworthy impression, landing, signup, and activation data to improve conversion and retention.

executionTarget.rationale: The canonical TradeScout repository owns public rendering, sitemap generation, profile eligibility, signup persistence, analytics, platform-law guards, and the Render production release path.
constraintsConsidered: The recovery depends on real routing, database-backed identity, server-confirmed registration, custom-domain configuration, and exact production build identity.
A standalone marketing site cannot correct the canonical application's crawl graph, signup truth, or Trust/CVS exposure boundary.
